Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jon Ruiz (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Redwood Product), Sofia Martinez (PhotonApps CTO), Ethan Cole (PhotonApps ML Eng), Priya Nair (PhotonApps SRE), Liam O'Connor (PhotonApps PM)
summary: Redwood delivered an Optimize walkthrough focused on quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8). Discussed quality vs latency/cost tradeoffs, typical workload signals that favor INT8 or FP8, and Redwood Optimize recommendations and tooling for A/B style evals. PhotonApps expressed interest in a short POC to benchmark their prompts; next steps defined to share benchmarks and run perf tests.
topics: Overview of Optimize and quantization profiles
When to prefer INT8 vs FP8
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll wait a minute for folks to pop in, um this is maya from redwood, and jon and carlos are with me.
[00:08] Sofia Martinez: Hi, Sofia here, sounds good.
[00:12] Jon Ruiz: nice to meet you all, i'll be doing the deep dive on quant profiles.
[00:18] Maya Patel: quick agenda, 1) what the optimize module is, 2) quant profiles INT8/FP8, 3) quality vs latency demos, 4) next steps and POC. fine to proceed?
[00:27] Ethan Cole: yep all good.
[00:30] Maya Patel: cool — jon, i'll hand over to you.
[00:33] Jon Ruiz: awesome. so high level, Optimize is our cost/perf toolkit that recommends batching, caching, and quantization profiles by workload. today we'll focus on quantization: INT8 and FP8, and tradeoffs.
[00:46] Jon Ruiz: quick note — our internal shorthand sometimes calls FP8 "eight-fp" or "f-p eight" so apologies if that comes out weird in the transcript.
[00:54] [01:00] Jon Ruiz: INT8 reduces model size and in many cases halves memory and increases throughput, but it can introduce more accuracy regression than FP8 depending on model/finetune. FP8 is newer, gives a better quality/latency sweet spot for a lot of decoder-only LLMs, but may need hardware support (A100/Blackwell-ish) or kernels we provide.
[01:25] Priya Nair: what about NVidia support — we have some on-prem A100s and planning Blackwell eval next quarter.
[01:33] Jon Ruiz: A100 is supported for both INT8 and FP8 in our runtime; for Blackwell we have early kernels, can run compat tests in the pilot. sometimes kernel availability changes perf numbers a bit.
[01:45] Sofia Martinez: can you show a side-by-side on quality vs latency? that's what our team cares about.
[01:51] Jon Ruiz: sure. i'll pull up a short demo: we ran a 1000 prompt eval across a mix of short chat and longer instruction prompts. chart 1 — baseline fp16 (floating 16) latency median ~150ms per token, quality baseline. INT8 reduced latency to ~90ms but BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics dropped more, especially on long-context instruction. FP8 latency ~110ms with small quality drop ~1-2% on our eval.
[02:20] [02:30] Maya Patel: worth emphasizing these numbers depend on sequence lengths, batch sizes, and your prompt distribution — you gave us some sample prompts earlier?
[02:40] Ethan Cole: we shared a handful, yes 10 prompts; we'll add more.
[02:45] Jon Ruiz: perfect. so the recommendation pattern: if you need aggressive cost savings and your workload is short-turn chat with lots of similar short tokens, INT8 gives best unit cost. If you need higher quality and long-form instructions or chain-of-thought, FP8 tends to preserve quality while still giving meaningful speedups.
[03:05] Carlos Vega: also Optimize surfaces per-route quant profile suggestions and can run A/B style evals automatically. you can pin a route to FP8 for the pilot and have fallback to fp16 if quality drifts.
[03:18] Sofia Martinez: how do we measure drift? we want alerts if quality drops.
[03:22] Jon Ruiz: Optimize ties into eval hooks — you give us reference outputs and metrics (e.g., exact match, BLEU, hallucination rate) and it will run regression tests and alert when thresholds cross. we also keep token-level traces to help triage.
[03:36] Priya Nair: any impacts on KV cache behavior with INT8? i've seen caching break in some quantized runtimes.
[03:43] Jon Ruiz: good call — our KV cache is preserved across quant modes at the runtime layer; we handle correct serialization and conversion at load time. occasional edge cases with very long contexts require small tweaks, we'll capture those in the POC run.
[03:58] [04:00] Ethan Cole: can you talk about model variants — like do we need a separate model for INT8 vs FP8?
[04:06] Jon Ruiz: usually we have a quantized artifact per profile. Redwood supports on-the-fly fallback to a compatible variant (we'll route to fp16 if fp8 not available). the storage overhead is usually modest compared to gains.
[04:20] Maya Patel: also architecture note — some model families quantize better, e.g., some open-weights decoder models have good INT8 stability while others prefer FP8.
[04:30] Sofia Martinez: would you recommend starting FP8 or INT8 for an ecommerce summarization workflow? we do product descriptions, long context.
[04:39] Jon Ruiz: for long context summarization — FP8 first. preserves quality on long passages, better for chain-of-thought. INT8 could be explored if cost pressure is very high and you accept slight quality hit.
[04:51] [05:00] Jon Ruiz: demo time — i'm switching to the Optimize console. bear with me while the screen shares.
[05:08] [05:30] Jon Ruiz: (screen) here is the Optimize dashboard — route-level suggestions, recommended quant profile, sample perf numbers and a button to run a quick A/B evaluation. clicking the A/B button runs N=200 sample prompts against currently selected profiles.
[05:45] Jon Ruiz: i'm kicking off an A/B run: fp16 vs fp8 vs int8. should take ~2 minutes for the sample.
[05:52] Maya Patel: while it runs, quick question — does your billing change by quant profile? like lower unit cost for INT8?
[05:58] Carlos Vega: yes we expose per-token unit economics by profile in the console and the pricing model reflects lower compute for quantized runs; billing is still per-token but your per-token compute multiplier differs.
[06:10] [06:30] Jon Ruiz: results coming in: latency median fp16 152ms, fp8 112ms, int8 88ms. quality scores (we use a composite metric here) fp16 0.87 baseline, fp8 0.85 (-0.02), int8 0.79 (-0.08).
[06:48] Ethan Cole: that's a notable drop for INT8. is that typical?
[06:52] Jon Ruiz: depends. on short-turn chat often INT8 is much closer to baseline; on instruction and long-context evals, we've seen larger deltas. your prompts will determine which profile is acceptable.
[07:05] [07:20] Sofia Martinez: what about ensemble approaches — can we route low-risk calls to INT8 and high-risk to FP8?
[07:26] Maya Patel: yes that's a frequent pattern — route by intent classifier or by token budget. Optimize can recommend routing rules and monitor end-to-end cost/quality.
[07:37] Priya Nair: curious about fallbacks — if int8 falls below threshold we want automatic fallback, does that add latency?
[07:44] Jon Ruiz: minimal. fallback is a routing decision before request hits the GPU; we keep a tiny warm pool of higher-precision variants for fast failover. so you'd see a small infrequent bump but not full cold-start.
[07:59] [08:10] Jon Ruiz: okay now i'll show a notebook run we did on a real customer dataset. note: these numbers are representative.
[08:18] Jon Ruiz: (screen) notebook shows per-prompt latency distributions, tokenization differences, and examples where int8 hallucinated more on named-entity heavy prompts.
[08:33] Ethan Cole: that aligns with our worry: we do product descriptions and named entities are critical.
[08:39] Jon Ruiz: then FP8 as a default is my recommendation; we can run an INT8 cost-savings pass on lower-risk endpoints.
[08:47] Maya Patel: we'll put that in the pilot scope.
[08:50] [09:00] Sofia Martinez: questions on security/compliance — if we run a pilot on your Hosted API, how is data handled?
[09:06] Maya Patel: Hosted keeps user data encrypted at rest and in transit; we have SOC2 and can do per-customer retention policies. for stricter needs we can run Dedicated or Private with VPC and KMS integrations.
[09:18] Priya Nair: good — we will likely ask for Private for PII.
[09:22] Maya Patel: noted. we'll include a security pack link in the follow-up (SOC2 report, PCI if relevant, KMS docs).
[09:29] [09:40] Jon Ruiz: another nuance — FP8 tends to be less brittle across finetunes. if you've trained custom models or instruction-tuned, FP8 saves you time. INT8 sometimes needs additional calibration/fine-tuning to stabilize.
[09:56] Ethan Cole: we have light instruction tuning on our base model. probably okay to test FP8 first.
[10:01] [10:20] Maya Patel: ok quick recap — recommended FP8 for long-context summarization, INT8 for short-chat cost pushes; Optimize can run per-route A/Bs and monitor; pilot next. any other questions?
[10:30] Sofia Martinez: what does the pilot look like? duration, scope?
[10:33] Maya Patel: typically 2 weeks, we 1) onboard sample prompts, 2) run A/B evals across profiles, 3) produce a report with per-token cost estimates and recommendation, and 4) optionally run a small traffic experiment.
[10:47] Liam O'Connor: will there be checkpoints during the two weeks?
[10:50] Jon Ruiz: weekly syncs and an end-of-pilot review, plus access to the Optimize dashboard and raw logs.
[10:57] [11:10] Sofia Martinez: pricing — can you ballpark savings?
[11:15] Carlos Vega: rough back-of-envelope: INT8 can reduce GPU compute cost per token by ~30-40% vs fp16 in many cases; FP8 around 15-25% depending on kernel and sequence length. we'll share a modelled spreadsheet.
[11:31] Ethan Cole: ok that's helpful.
[11:35] [11:40] Priya Nair: any instability concerns for production? we care about reliability.
[11:43] Jon Ruiz: production is our focus — we provide rollout controls (canary percent, auto-fallback, saturation limits) and observability. most customers run FP8 in production with safeguards.
[11:56] [12:10] Maya Patel: i'm going to capture next steps here — we'll send the benchmark spreadsheet, and jon will run a sample INT8/FP8 eval on your provided prompts.
[12:20] Ethan Cole: we'll add 5 more prompts and share eval criteria by monday.
[12:24] Sofia Martinez: and we'll scope Private versus Hosted in parallel — security team will evaluate.
[12:30] [12:40] Jon Ruiz: any vendor lock questions — customers ask about model portability. we support exporting quantized artifacts and provide model variant docs.
[12:50] Maya Patel: also to note, if you choose Dedicated, you get reserved capacity which makes latency more predictable with quantization.
[13:01] [13:20] Sofia Martinez: one last question — for hallucination metrics, do you support custom detectors?
[13:26] Jon Ruiz: yes you can plug in your own eval functions or use our built-in heuristics; Optimize will run them as part of the regression checks.
[13:34] Maya Patel: great, unless there's anything else we'll wrap. thank you all for your time.
[13:40] Sofia Martinez: thanks, very useful.
[13:44] Ethan Cole: thanks team.
[13:47] Priya Nair: thanks.
[13:50] Maya Patel: we'll follow up with materials and a proposed pilot kickoff calendar.
[13:56] [14:00] Meeting end: 15:18 UTC — recording stopped.

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription errors for product names (FP8 sometimes appears as "F P eight") and kernel/hardware names, and speaker turns may be off by a line or two.
